messages:
Mia Chen: Following up on the routing-policy RFC — thinking we should split policy evaluation into a two-phase pipeline: a cheap stateless filter to eliminate obviously-incompatible routes, then a secondary scorer that can use heavier telemetry and tenant constraints. Thoughts? :thinking:

Raj Patel: I like the two-phase idea. it buys us predictable p99 for the common case (filter pass) and keeps expensive work for fewer candidates. question: where's the boundary? do we expose a typed metadata bag to the scorer or keep it in runtime-only?

Alex Gomez: boundary matters for caching. if the filter outputs a small set of route ids we can cache KV entries per (route, model-version) and avoid re-running scorer for replays. exposing too much runtime context in the scorer will make cache keys explode.

Sasha Lee: agree w/ Alex. also need explainability hooks in the scorer for evals/regressions. We should require the scorer to emit a lightweight explanation object (reason codes + score components). that lets Optimize and Console display drop-in insights.

Mia Chen: proposal: filter = pure function(req_meta) -> Set[route_id]. scorer = plugin(route_id, request_context, optional precomputed telemetry) -> {score, explanation}. runtime ensures scorer gets only preapproved telemetry keys (privacy + cost). keeps interface small.

Raj Patel: that API feels OK. small nit: "optional precomputed telemetry" implies we run background collectors and may not have values at request time. scorer must handle missing keys gracefully. please add a versioned schema for telemetry keys.

Alex Gomez: also: we should codify which parts of the scoring are allowed to be non-deterministic or time-dependent. e.g., latency estimates may vary; those should be marked as volatile so caching ignores them.

Sasha Lee: agreed. and add a deterministic path for canary rollouts: scorer should accept a stable seed for hashed decisions so A/B can reproduce decisions in logs.

Mia Chen: example interface sketch: 
```
interface Filter {
  filter(req_meta: Map[string,string]) -> List[string] // route ids
}
interface Scorer {
  score(route_id: string, ctx: RequestCtx, telemetry: Map[string,float] | null, seed: string | null) -> {score: float, reason: string} 
}
```
This keeps things simple and serializable.

Raj Patel: migration plan? we have a bunch of legacy policies that assume a monolithic eval. how do we transition without a big blast radius?

Mia Chen: plan: 1) implement shim adaptor that runs legacy policy as a scorer behind a filter layer (filter defaults to all routes). 2) add telemetry facade that translates old metrics to new keys. 3) staged rollout per tenant with feature-flagged path. 4) telemetry-driven health checks to auto-rollback.

Alex Gomez: +1. add a opt-in sim-mode where we run new filter+scorer in shadow and compare decisions for N days before flip. saves surprises.

Sasha Lee: ops checklist additions: explainability traces in logs, histogram of "filter candidate count" per request, tail-latency per scorer, and an alert if candidate_count increases 2x after rollout.

infra-bot: deploy:policy-shim v0.1 deployed to canary cluster (canary-3) at 2026-03-21T14:02Z :rocket:

Mia Chen: perfect. next actions: Raj to draft the telemetry key schema + validation rules; Alex to prototype route-id caching layer; Sasha to add explainability contract to the scorer interface. I'll collect a migration playbook and write the follow-up RFC update. :thumbsup:
